_about: Money Quest quote series. `verification` must be "verified" before a video can be produced. All quotations except three were checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text of the original work; Dewey (1897), Clear and Kahneman were confirmed from transcriptions or the author's own published text. Never change `quote` without re-verifying. `rights` records why the quotation may be used. No quoted author endorses Money Quest.

rejected.quote: An investment in knowledge pays the best interest.
rejected.reason: Not found in Franklin's papers or in any publication before 1818; reference works list it as unverified.
Dweck has said the saying predates her; not presented as her quotation.

quotes.pillar: Financial literacy and healthy money habits
quotes.hook: Where does your child's pocket money go?
quotes.quote: Beware of little expenses; a small leak will sink a great ship.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.source: Benjamin Franklin, "The Way to Wealth" (Father Abraham's speech, preface to Poor Richard Improved, 1758).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #20203) on 16 November 2026. Spelling modernised from "Expences"; capitalisation normalised.
quotes.takeaway: Small spending choices add up. Children can learn to notice them.
quotes.cta: Try the spending activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Franklin wrote this in 1758, and it still fits a child's pocket money. Small, everyday spending choices are where money habits begin. Noticing them is a skill children can practise.

quotes.hook: Does your child give up when things get hard?
quotes.quote: I'm not afraid of storms, for I'm learning how to sail my ship.
quotes.author: Louisa May Alcott
quotes.source: Louisa May Alcott, Little Women, Part Second (1869), chapter 44. Spoken by the character Amy.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #514) on 16 November 2026. Spoken by the character Amy in chapter 44.
quotes.takeaway: Resilience grows through practice, not perfection.
quotes.cta: Try the Emotion Lab activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Amy says this near the end of Little Women. Resilience isn't the absence of difficulty. It's the growing sense that you can handle it, and children build that sense through small, safe practice.

quotes.pillar: Psychology of learning and child development
quotes.hook: How do children really learn about money?
quotes.quote: Education … is a process of living and not a preparation for future living.
quotes.author: John Dewey
quotes.source: John Dewey, "My Pedagogic Creed", The School Journal, vol. 54 (16 January 1897), Article I. Full sentence: "I believe that education, therefore, is a process of living and not a preparation for future living."
quotes.verification_note: Confirmed in multiple transcriptions of the 1897 text. The ellipsis marks the omitted word "therefore". The popular version "Education is life itself" is a paraphrase and is not used.
quotes.takeaway: Children learn by doing, one real choice at a time.
quotes.cta: Try a Real Life Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Dewey's point from 1897: learning isn't a rehearsal for later. Children learn when they take part in real things now, like choosing, planning and trying, with support.

quotes.hook: How do you raise a responsible child?
quotes.quote: Few things help an individual more than to place responsibility upon him, and to let him know that you trust him.
quotes.author: Booker T. Washington
quotes.source: Booker T. Washington, Up from Slavery: An Autobiography (1901), chapter XI.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #2376) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Trust and small responsibilities help children grow.
quotes.cta: Try Leadership Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Washington wrote this about running a school, and it holds for a family too. A small, real responsibility, given with trust, is one of the simplest ways to help a child grow.

quotes.hook: Why does that toy feel so urgent right now?
quotes.quote: Nothing in life is as important as you think it is, while you are thinking about it.
quotes.author: Daniel Kahneman
quotes.source: Daniel Kahneman, "Focusing Illusion", Edge.org annual question essay (2011); the idea is developed in Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011), chapter 38.
quotes.verification_note: Wording confirmed from Kahneman's own Edge essay. The book's chapter 38 wording should be checked if the book is cited alone.
quotes.rights: In copyright. One short sentence quoted with attribution for education and commentary; no endorsement implied.
quotes.takeaway: A short pause helps children choose with care.
quotes.cta: Try the Brain Lab activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: In the moment, the thing a child wants can feel like the only thing that matters. Adults feel it too. A short pause before deciding is a habit worth practising together.

quotes.hook: Is your child afraid of getting it wrong?
quotes.quote: We often discover what will do, by finding out what will not do; and probably he who never made a mistake never made a discovery.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Samuel Smiles, Self-Help; with Illustrations of Conduct and Perseverance (1859), chapter XI.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #935) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Testing an idea, and learning from it, is how children create.
quotes.cta: Try Entrepreneur Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Every young inventor needs to hear this. An idea that doesn't work is information, not failure. Children learn to create by testing small ideas and trying again.

quotes.hook: Why do small things feel so big to children?
quotes.quote: Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: Epictetus, The Encheiridion, section V, translated by George Long (1877).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #10661) on 16 November 2026. The sentence continues with an example, omitted here.
quotes.takeaway: Children can learn to notice a feeling before they act.
quotes.cta: Try the Emotion Lab activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: An idea almost two thousand years old: what we tell ourselves about an event shapes how it feels. Children can learn to notice a feeling and choose a next step.

quotes.hook: What does that toy really cost your child?
quotes.quote: The cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it, immediately or in the long run.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.source: Henry David Thoreau, Walden (1854), "Economy".
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #205) on 16 November 2026. The sentence begins mid-clause in the original; the first letter is capitalised.
quotes.takeaway: Children can learn to ask what a purchase really costs.
quotes.cta: Try the budgeting activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Thoreau measured cost in life, not money: the time and effort something takes to earn. It's a useful question for a child weighing a purchase against a savings goal.

quotes.hook: What is the one skill your child will always need?
quotes.quote: The object and reward of learning is continued capacity for growth.
quotes.author: John Dewey
quotes.source: John Dewey, Democracy and Education (1916), chapter eight, "Aims in Education".
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #852) on 16 November 2026. The clause follows "or that" in the original; the first letter is capitalised.
quotes.takeaway: Learning how to keep learning is a skill for life.
quotes.cta: Try the Future Skills activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: For Dewey, the point of learning was the ability to keep learning. That matters even more for children growing up with tools that change every year.

quotes.pillar: Financial literacy and healthy money habits
quotes.hook: Can one coin a week change a habit?
quotes.quote: Every action you take is a vote for the type of person you wish to become.
quotes.author: James Clear
quotes.source: James Clear, Atomic Habits (Avery, 2018), chapter 2.
quotes.verification_note: Confirmed on the author's own site, which publishes the chapter 2 excerpt and repeats the sentence.
quotes.rights: In copyright. One short sentence quoted with attribution for education and commentary; no endorsement implied.
quotes.takeaway: Small habits, repeated, build confidence.
quotes.cta: Try the saving activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: A coin in a jar is a small thing. Repeated every week, it becomes evidence a child can point to: "I'm someone who saves."

quotes.hook: Can small savings really reach a big goal?
quotes.quote: Little strokes fell great oaks.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.source: Benjamin Franklin, "The Way to Wealth" (1758), quoting his earlier Poor Richard's Almanack.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #20203) on 16 November 2026. Capitalisation normalised.
quotes.takeaway: Small savings, repeated, reach big goals.
quotes.cta: Set a savings goal on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: One small step doesn't look like much. Franklin's point is that many of them do the work. A savings goal lets a child see that for themselves.

quotes.pillar: Psychology of learning and child development
quotes.hook: Why do early habits matter so much?
quotes.quote: The great thing in all education is to make our nervous system our ally instead of our enemy.
quotes.author: William James
quotes.source: William James, Talks to Teachers on Psychology (1899), chapter VIII, "The Laws of Habit".
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #16287) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Good habits, started early, make later choices easier.
quotes.cta: Try a Real Life Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: William James argued that habits do much of the work for us, for better or worse. Small routines practised in childhood, like saving a coin or checking a list, become things a child no longer has to think about.

quotes.hook: How do children learn to trust themselves?
quotes.quote: Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, "Self-Reliance", in Essays (1841).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #2944) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Confidence grows when children make real choices.
quotes.cta: Try the Money Simulator on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Self-trust isn't something we can hand to a child. It comes from making real decisions and seeing what happens, ideally where mistakes cost nothing.

quotes.hook: Are you doing too much for your child?
quotes.quote: No one can be free unless he is independent.
quotes.author: Maria Montessori
quotes.source: Maria Montessori, The Montessori Method (1912), chapter V, translated by Anne E. George.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #39863) on 16 November 2026. The sentence continues after a colon in the original.
quotes.takeaway: Independence is built one small responsibility at a time.
quotes.cta: Try a Real Life Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Montessori saw independence as the first goal of education. At home it can start small: one job, one decision, one thing a child manages alone.

quotes.hook: How do you raise a kind child?
quotes.quote: No one is useless in this world who lightens the burden of it for any one else.
quotes.author: Charles Dickens
quotes.source: Charles Dickens, Our Mutual Friend (1865), Book the Third, chapter 9. Spoken by John Rokesmith.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #883) on 16 November 2026. In the novel the line is interrupted by "retorted the Secretary"; the narration is omitted.
quotes.takeaway: Kindness and giving are skills children can practise.
quotes.cta: Try the giving activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: A line from Dickens that children understand straight away: helping someone matters. Giving time, a toy or a little money is a habit that can start young.

quotes.pillar: Financial literacy and healthy money habits
quotes.hook: Is money in charge, or is your child?
quotes.quote: Money is in some respects like fire; it is a very excellent servant but a terrible master.
quotes.author: P. T. Barnum
quotes.source: P. T. Barnum, The Art of Money Getting; or, Golden Rules for Making Money (1880).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #8581) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Children can learn that money is a tool to manage.
quotes.cta: Try the money basics activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Barnum's image still works: money is useful when you direct it. Children can practise being the one in charge, with small amounts and real choices.

quotes.hook: What do you say after your child's mistake?
quotes.quote: Isn't it nice to think that tomorrow is a new day with no mistakes in it yet?
quotes.author: L. M. Montgomery
quotes.source: L. M. Montgomery, Anne of Green Gables (1908), chapter XXI. Spoken by Anne.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #45) on 16 November 2026. The line follows "Marilla," in the original; the first letter is capitalised.
quotes.takeaway: A mistake is a place to start again.
quotes.cta: Try the Emotion Lab activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Anne says this after a very bad day. It's a kind thing to tell a child, and a useful one: tomorrow is a chance to try differently.

quotes.hook: Does your child memorise, or understand?
quotes.quote: Learning without thought is labour lost; thought without learning is perilous.
quotes.author: Confucius
quotes.source: Confucius, The Analects, translated by James Legge (1861).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #3330) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Children learn more when they stop and think it through.
quotes.cta: Try the Brain Lab activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Facts without thinking don't stick, and opinions without facts go wrong. Asking a child "why do you think that?" trains both at once.

quotes.hook: What is the simplest budget rule of all?
quotes.quote: Annual income twenty pounds, annual expenditure nineteen nineteen and six, result happiness.
quotes.author: Charles Dickens
quotes.source: Charles Dickens, David Copperfield (1850), chapter 12. Spoken by Mr. Micawber.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #766) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Spending a little less than you have is a skill.
quotes.cta: Try the spending activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Mr. Micawber's rule is the whole of budgeting in one line: spend slightly less than comes in. Children can practise it with pocket money long before they earn a wage.

quotes.hook: What does your child do when something is missing?
quotes.quote: Necessity is the mother of invention.
quotes.author: Aesop
quotes.source: Aesop, "The Crow and the Pitcher", in Three Hundred Aesop's Fables, translated by George Fyler Townsend (1867).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #21) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: A problem is often where a good idea begins.
quotes.cta: Try Entrepreneur Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: The thirsty crow in the fable drops pebbles into a pitcher to raise the water. A child who faces a small problem, and is given time, will often invent a way through.

quotes.hook: How do children learn to care about others?
quotes.quote: What do we live for, if it is not to make life less difficult to each other?
quotes.author: George Eliot
quotes.source: George Eliot, Middlemarch (1871-72), Book VIII, chapter 72. Spoken by Dorothea.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #145) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Helping others is a habit children can build.
quotes.cta: Try the giving activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Dorothea asks this in Middlemarch, and it's a fair question for a family. Small acts of help, noticed and named, teach children that other people matter.

quotes.pillar: Financial literacy and healthy money habits
quotes.hook: Are children born knowing how to save?
quotes.quote: Economy is not a natural instinct, but the growth of experience, example, and forethought.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Samuel Smiles, Thrift (1875), chapter I.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #14418) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Good money habits are learned, mostly by example.
quotes.cta: Try the saving activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Nobody is born careful with money. Smiles put it down to experience, example and thinking ahead, which is good news: all three can be given to a child.

quotes.pillar: Psychology of learning and child development
quotes.hook: Why doesn't telling children always work?
quotes.quote: Education is not an affair of "telling" and being told, but an active and constructive process.
quotes.author: John Dewey
quotes.source: John Dewey, Democracy and Education (1916), chapter three.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #852) on 16 November 2026. The sentence begins "That education is not"; the first letter is capitalised.
quotes.takeaway: Children understand what they have worked out themselves.
quotes.cta: Try a Real Life Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Dewey noticed that everyone agrees with this and few act on it. A child told about saving nods. A child who saves for something learns it.

quotes.hook: Does your child lead by pushing or by listening?
quotes.quote: Persuasion is better than Force.
quotes.author: Aesop
quotes.source: Aesop, "The North Wind and the Sun", in Three Hundred Aesop's Fables, translated by George Fyler Townsend (1867).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #21) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Good leaders win people over. They don't push.
quotes.cta: Try Leadership Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: In the fable the sun does what the wind could not. Children meet the same choice in every group game: insist, or bring people with you.

quotes.hook: Does your child believe they can improve?
quotes.quote: Optimism is the faith that leads to achievement; nothing can be done without hope.
quotes.author: Helen Keller
quotes.source: Helen Keller, Optimism: An Essay (1903), Part III.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #31622) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Hope gives children a reason to keep trying.
quotes.cta: Try the Emotion Lab activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Keller wrote this at 23. A child who expects that effort can change things is more willing to make the effort, and that expectation can be encouraged.

quotes.hook: Does your child jump to conclusions?
quotes.quote: The essence of critical thinking is suspended judgment.
quotes.author: John Dewey
quotes.source: John Dewey, How We Think (1910), chapter six.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #37423) on 16 November 2026. The sentence continues after a semicolon in the original.
quotes.takeaway: Waiting before deciding is a thinking skill.
quotes.cta: Try the Brain Lab activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Critical thinking starts with not deciding too fast. "Let's find out first" is a habit a child can practise on adverts, rumours and big purchases.

quotes.hook: How does a child reach a big savings goal?
quotes.quote: The journey of a thousand li commenced with a single step.
quotes.author: Lao Tzu
quotes.source_line: Tao Te Ching, trans. James Legge
quotes.source: Lao Tzu, Tao Te Ching, translated by James Legge (1891). A li is a traditional Chinese unit of distance.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #216) on 16 November 2026. The clause follows a semicolon in the original; the first letter is capitalised.
quotes.takeaway: Every big goal starts with one small step.
quotes.cta: Set a savings goal on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: A big goal can look impossible to a child. The first coin in the jar is the single step, and it makes the second one easier.

quotes.hook: Which three habits build a learner for life?
quotes.quote: Reading maketh a full man; conference a ready man; and writing an exact man.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon
quotes.source: Francis Bacon, "Of Studies", in Essays (1625).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #575) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Reading, talking and writing each build a different skill.
quotes.cta: Explore the Library on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Four hundred years on, Bacon's list holds up: reading fills the mind, discussion sharpens it, writing makes it precise. Children need all three.

quotes.hook: Do you do things your child could do?
quotes.quote: We habitually serve children; and this is not only an act of servility toward them, but it is dangerous, since it tends to suffocate their useful, spontaneous activity.
quotes.author: Maria Montessori
quotes.source: Maria Montessori, The Montessori Method (1912), chapter V, translated by Anne E. George.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #39863) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Stepping back lets children practise doing things themselves.
quotes.cta: Try a Real Life Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Montessori is blunt here. Doing everything for a child feels kind, but it removes the practice they need. One task handed over this week is a start.

quotes.pillar: Financial literacy and healthy money habits
quotes.hook: Need it, or just want it?
quotes.quote: Buy what thou hast no need of, and ere long thou shalt sell thy necessaries.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.source: Benjamin Franklin, "The Way to Wealth" (1758).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #20203) on 16 November 2026. Capitalisation normalised.
quotes.takeaway: Telling needs from wants protects what matters most.
quotes.cta: Try the spending activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Franklin's warning in plain words: spend on what you don't need and you may run short of what you do. Sorting needs from wants is one of the first money skills.

quotes.hook: What happens to the thoughts your child repeats?
quotes.quote: Where you tend a rose, my lad, a thistle cannot grow.
quotes.author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
quotes.source: Frances Hodgson Burnett, The Secret Garden (1911), chapter 27.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #113) on 16 November 2026. Two lines of verse in the original, joined here.
quotes.takeaway: The thoughts children practise are the ones that grow.
quotes.cta: Try the Emotion Lab activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Burnett's point is about attention: a mind busy with something good has less room for something bad. Children can learn to choose what they tend.

quotes.hook: What is your child excited to make?
quotes.quote: Nothing great was ever achieved without enthusiasm.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, "Circles", in Essays (1841).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #2944) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: A child's own interest is where real projects begin.
quotes.cta: Try Entrepreneur Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Enthusiasm isn't a distraction from learning. It's the fuel. A child's own idea, however small, is worth taking seriously enough to try.

quotes.pillar: Psychology of learning and child development
quotes.hook: What actually changes how a child behaves?
quotes.quote: Education is for behavior, and habits are the stuff of which behavior consists.
quotes.author: William James
quotes.source: William James, Talks to Teachers on Psychology (1899), chapter VIII, "The Laws of Habit".
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #16287) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Small habits, repeated, shape how children act.
quotes.cta: Try a Real Life Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: James thought the test of education was what a person does, not what they can recite. For children that means practice: the same small thing, many times.

quotes.hook: Does your child want everything right now?
quotes.quote: Slow but steady wins the race.
quotes.author: Aesop
quotes.source: Aesop, "The Hare and the Tortoise", in Three Hundred Aesop's Fables, translated by George Fyler Townsend (1867).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #21) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Saving a little, regularly, gets children there.
quotes.cta: Try the saving activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: The tortoise never stops, and that's the whole lesson. A small amount saved every week beats a big burst that fades.

quotes.hook: Does your child believe what looks convincing?
quotes.quote: Take nothing on its looks; take everything on evidence. There's no better rule.
quotes.author: Charles Dickens
quotes.source: Charles Dickens, Great Expectations (1861), chapter 40. Spoken by Mr. Jaggers.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #1400) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Children can learn to ask for evidence.
quotes.cta: Try the Future Skills activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Mr. Jaggers is a lawyer, but his rule suits anyone online. A confident video or a shiny advert isn't evidence. "How do we know?" is the question to practise.

quotes.hook: Is your child afraid to try something new?
quotes.quote: True courage is in facing danger when you are afraid.
quotes.author: L. Frank Baum
quotes.source: L. Frank Baum, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), chapter 15. Spoken by Oz to the Cowardly Lion.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #55) on 16 November 2026. The sentence continues in the original.
quotes.takeaway: Being brave means trying while still feeling nervous.
quotes.cta: Try the Emotion Lab activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Oz tells the Lion that fear and courage go together. Children often think brave people don't feel scared. It helps to tell them otherwise.

quotes.pillar: Financial literacy and healthy money habits
quotes.hook: Does your child know what things really cost?
quotes.quote: The real price of every thing, what every thing really costs to the man who wants to acquire it, is the toil and trouble of acquiring it.
quotes.author: Adam Smith
quotes.source: Adam Smith, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations (1776), Book I, chapter V.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #3300) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Children can learn that money stands for effort.
quotes.cta: Try the money basics activities on Money Quest.

quotes.hook: How do children learn to manage their time?
quotes.quote: Have regular hours for work and play, make each day both useful and pleasant, and prove that you understand the worth of time by employing it well.
quotes.author: Louisa May Alcott
quotes.source: Louisa May Alcott, Little Women (1868), chapter 11. Spoken by Mrs. March.

quotes.takeaway: A simple routine helps children plan their own day.
quotes.cta: Try the planning activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Mrs. March says this after her daughters try a week with no duties at all. Children who help plan their own day start to feel that time is theirs to use.

quotes.hook: Is "I already know" stopping your child?
quotes.quote: It is impossible for a man to begin to learn that which he thinks that he knows.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: Epictetus, Discourses, translated by George Long (1877).

quotes.takeaway: Staying curious keeps children open to learning.
quotes.cta: Try the Future Skills activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: "I know!" can close a conversation. Children learn more when they get used to checking, asking and being pleasantly wrong.

quotes.hook: Why should children think about tomorrow?
quotes.quote: Thrift began with civilization. It began when men found it necessary to provide for to-morrow, as well as for to-day.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Samuel Smiles, Thrift (1875), chapter I.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #14418) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Planning ahead is a skill children can practise.
quotes.cta: Try the planning activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Saving is thinking about your future self. For a child that might be next Saturday, which is a perfectly good place to begin.

quotes.pillar: Psychology of learning and child development
quotes.hook: Trying to change your child's habit overnight?
quotes.quote: Habit is habit, and not to be flung out of the window by any man, but coaxed down-stairs a step at a time.
quotes.author: Mark Twain
quotes.source: Mark Twain, The Tragedy of Pudd'nhead Wilson (1894), chapter 6 epigraph, "Pudd'nhead Wilson's Calendar".
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #102) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Habits change gently, one small step at a time.
quotes.cta: Try a Real Life Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Twain is joking, and he's right. A habit rarely changes by force. One small change, kept up, works better than a big new rule.

quotes.hook: What makes giving feel good to a child?
quotes.quote: Those who are happiest are those who do the most for others.
quotes.author: Booker T. Washington
quotes.source: Booker T. Washington, Up from Slavery: An Autobiography (1901), chapter IV.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #2376) on 16 November 2026. The clause follows "learning that" in the original; the first letter is capitalised.
quotes.takeaway: Giving is something children can practise and enjoy.
quotes.cta: Try the giving activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Washington learned this as a student and said he carried it for life. Children find it out the same way, by helping and seeing the result.

quotes.hook: Who is your child's most important teacher?
quotes.quote: The best part of every man's education is that which he gives to himself.
quotes.author: Sir Walter Scott
quotes.source: Sir Walter Scott, as quoted by Samuel Smiles in Self-Help (1859), chapter XI.

quotes.takeaway: Learning independently is a skill for life.

quotes.caption: School ends. Teaching yourself doesn't. A child who has looked something up, tried it and worked it out has started the habit that matters most.

quotes.hook: Does your child only work for rewards?
quotes.quote: The reward of a thing well done, is to have done it.
quotes.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.source: Ralph Waldo Emerson, "New England Reformers", in Essays: Second Series (1844).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #2945) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Pride in finishing something is its own reward.

quotes.caption: Stickers and prizes fade. The feeling of "I did that" lasts. It helps to notice the effort and the finished thing, more than the prize.

quotes.hook: Is "I'll do it later" a daily phrase?
quotes.quote: Never do tomorrow what you can do today. Procrastination is the thief of time.
quotes.author: Charles Dickens
quotes.source: Charles Dickens, David Copperfield (1850), chapter 12. Spoken by Mr. Micawber.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #766) on 16 November 2026. The first letter is capitalised.
quotes.takeaway: Starting small today builds responsibility.
quotes.cta: Try the planning activities on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Mr. Micawber gives excellent advice he never follows. For children, the trick is making the first step tiny enough to do now.

quotes.pillar: Psychology of learning and child development
quotes.hook: What does your child see you do with money?
quotes.quote: Childhood is like a mirror, which reflects in after-life the images first presented to it.
quotes.author: Samuel Smiles
quotes.source: Samuel Smiles, Character (1871), chapter II.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #2541) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Children learn most from what they see at home.
quotes.cta: Try a Real Life Quest on Money Quest.
quotes.caption: Children copy what they watch. Talking out loud about an everyday money choice, even a small one, is a lesson they'll remember.

quotes.pillar: Psychology of learning and child development
quotes.hook: Why does learning feel easier as a game?
quotes.quote: Work consists of whatever a body is obliged to do, and … Play consists of whatever a body is not obliged to do.
quotes.author: Mark Twain
quotes.source: Mark Twain, The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (1876), chapter 2.

quotes.takeaway: Children learn willingly when it feels like play.

quotes.hook: What can your child actually control?
quotes.quote: Of things some are in our power, and others are not.
quotes.author: Epictetus
quotes.source: Epictetus, The Encheiridion, section I, translated by George Long (1877).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #10661) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Children cope better when they focus on what they control.

quotes.caption: The first line of a very old handbook. A child can't control the weather or the result of the match, but they can control their effort and their next step.

quotes.hook: Is success just luck?
quotes.quote: Diligence is the mother of good luck.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.source: Benjamin Franklin, "The Way to Wealth" (1758).

quotes.hook: How many questions did your child ask today?
quotes.quote: The wisest of the Greeks used to say that wonder is the mother of all science.
quotes.author: John Dewey
quotes.source: John Dewey, How We Think (1910), chapter three.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #37423) on 16 November 2026.

quotes.hook: Too many small wants, no big goal?
quotes.quote: Our life is frittered away by detail.
quotes.author: Henry David Thoreau
quotes.source: Henry David Thoreau, Walden (1854).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #205) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Choosing fewer things leaves room for what matters.
quotes.cta: Set a savings goal on Money Quest.

quotes.hook: Does your child avoid anything difficult?
quotes.quote: Keep the faculty of effort alive in you by a little gratuitous exercise every day.
quotes.author: William James
quotes.source: William James, Talks to Teachers on Psychology (1899), chapter VIII, "The Laws of Habit".

quotes.takeaway: A little daily effort makes hard things easier.

quotes.hook: Does your child feel defined by yesterday's mistake?
quotes.quote: It's no use going back to yesterday, because I was a different person then.
quotes.author: Lewis Carroll
quotes.source: Lewis Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865), chapter 10. Spoken by Alice.
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #11) on 16 November 2026. The first letter is capitalised.
quotes.takeaway: Children change and grow every single day.

quotes.quote: Human felicity is produced not so much by great pieces of good fortune that seldom happen, as by little advantages that occur every day.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.source: Benjamin Franklin, Autobiography (first published 1791).
quotes.verification_note: Wording checked word for word against the Project Gutenberg text (ebook #20203) on 16 November 2026.
quotes.takeaway: Small everyday habits add up to a good life.

quotes.caption: Franklin thought happiness came from small daily advantages, not rare big wins. Money works the same way for children: the weekly habit matters more than the windfall.
